The duplicate creation path is in [topics.js](/app/src/controllers/write/topics.js:19): each request enters `api.topics.create` without a per-user guard. The post delay check in [user/posts.js](/app/src/user/posts.js:8) can read the same `lastposttime` for overlapping requests, allowing each to reach topic creation and increment the counters.

The likely fix is a lock acquired before the controller’s first `await`, keyed by authenticated `uid` or guest `sessionID`, and released in `finally`. A collision should throw the supplied error. The route already converts controller errors to HTTP 400 with `status.code: "bad-request"`; a successful 200 has `status.code: "ok"`. The lock’s behavior across multiple server processes remains uncertain.

I recorded the findings in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). Project source and tests were not changed because this run’s specialist instructions limit it to fault localization.

Added `lockPosting` to the topic controller. Create and reply requests now share a per-user or guest-session lock, and overlapping requests are rejected with HTTP 400 and `status.code: "bad-request"`. The lock is released in `finally`.

A new concurrency test confirms one request returns HTTP 200 with `status.code: "ok"`, four overlapping requests are rejected, and the global, category, and user topic counts each increase by one. ESLint and the targeted tests pass.

The lock is process-local; deployments with multiple server processes need a shared lock to enforce the same behavior across processes.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** [topics.js](/app/src/controllers/write/topics.js:14) stores posting locks in a process-local `Set`. [loader.js](/app/loader.js:116) can start multiple workers, so overlapping requests from the same user can reach different workers, both acquire a lock, and create duplicate topics. Use an atomic lock shared across workers, with safe release, and verify the concurrent request case across workers.

**Tests:** `./node_modules/.bin/mocha test/topics.js --grep "should accept only one concurrent topic creation"` passed (1 test), and `./node_modules/.bin/mocha test/topics.js` passed (230 tests). Both ran in one worker and do not cover the defect.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** The first focused run failed before any test with `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379`. Starting the installed local Redis service allowed both commands above to pass. I made no project code or test changes during this independent review.
